answer.why_different: The generated side omits the entire callback structure, so this is a different structure rather than merely a different value or address. The omission removes the callback notification contract from the PUT operation.
answer.spec_3gpp: The supplied 3GPP evidence defines notification types and notification payload concepts, including notifyMOIDeletion, notifyMOIAttributeValueChanges, and notifyMOIChanges, but it does not explicitly describe this callback location.
answer.openapi: The OpenAPI reference defines operation callbacks as a map of callback objects and defines each callback expression as a Path Item Object describing the callback request and expected responses. The official callback therefore represents a valid documented callback contract; omitting it loses that contract.
answer.clearer_why: The official version shows when and where the notification callback is invoked and documents its request and responses. The generated version provides no callback information.

evidence.text:
```
expression = ( "$url" | "$method" | "$statusCode" | "$request." source | "$response." source )
source = ( header-reference | query-reference | path-reference | body-reference )
header-reference = "header." token
query-reference = "query." name
path-reference = "path." name
body-reference = "body" ["#" fragment]
fragment = a JSON Pointer [RFC 6901](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6901)
name = *( char )
char = as per RFC [7159](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7159#section-7)
token = as per RFC [7230](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc7230#section-3.2.6)
```  
The `name` identifier is case-sensitive, whereas `token` is not.
